title: Local Minimax Risk for Three-State Curves from Designed Stationary Cross Sections
banked_reason: Math passes, but the delivered package is incremental with paper_score_ceiling 5.7 below the field threshold 7.4 and salvageable=false.
gap_reasons: It does not evaluate that cone risk, provide an attaining local procedure, or transfer the unrestricted Gaussian value to finite samples, so the advertised complete three-state decision problem remains open.
Its honest bands have the global root-N width order but no optimal-width result, and it proves no risk-optimal hazard or allocation design.

proof_attempt_summary: The run proved rank-free inverse stability, a matching fixed-dimension N^-1 squared-risk rate, a compact local Gaussian likelihood-process limit, and an exact additive decomposition of the six-dimensional minimax problem into regular variance plus a three-dimensional cone risk. The field-tier program collapsed at the nonlinear residual cone problem: no evaluated minimax value, certified attaining rule and lower certificate, or compact-to-finite-sample transfer was obtained. Sharp expected-width bands and globally certified hazard/allocation design therefore remain downstream open problems.
tldr: For each fixed interior noncyclic three-state baseline and legal hidden fiber, three designed stationary categorical cross sections yield an exact Gaussian reduction: the scalar local minimax risk equals an explicit regular variance plus a three-dimensional two-cone decision risk. Rank-free global stability and compact local likelihood convergence are established. The residual cone value, optimal honest curve band, finite-sample minimax transfer, and risk-optimal reset design remain open.
gap: Existing reset theory gives the forward observation law, while nonconvex inference and rational design theory do not yield the exact nonlinear local risk or band width for this unidentified fiber.
fill: Establish rank-free uniform recovery; for each fixed legal \((A,B,\rho,K)\), solve the compact-local-to-unbounded Gaussian minimax and simultaneous-band games with matching bounds; and derive a certifiable three-regime design for the resulting risk.
